description.value: The study examined how motivational dispositions measured by BIS/BAS scales modulate neural responses during cognitive reappraisal of positive and negative emotional stimuli in currently drug-free patients with major depressive disorder compared with healthy controls.

design.value: A block-design fMRI study compared 12 currently drug-free major depressed outpatients with 15 healthy controls during three consecutive emotion-regulation conditions: ATTEND, DETACH, and IMMERSE. DETACH and IMMERSE order was counterbalanced across participants, and positive, negative, and neutral affective pictures were presented.

task_description.value: Participants performed three consecutive blocks: ATTEND, DETACH, and IMMERSE. During ATTEND, subjects responded naturally without trying to change the emotional state. During DETACH, participants interpreted the situation as fake or unreal. During IMMERSE, subjects perceived each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.

instructions.value: ATTEND: respond naturally without trying to change the emotional state. DETACH: interpret the situation depicted as fake or unreal, as would someone with no personal attachment to the events. IMMERSE: perceive each picture as real by imagining yourself or a loved one in the scene.

stimuli.value: Pictures selected from the International Affective Picture System; positive, negative, and neutral affective pictures.

task_performance_measures.value: self-reported ratings of emotional intensity on a 4-point Likert scale

instrument.value: Siemens 3T Tim Trio MRI system (Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: Three functional sessions were acquired. Functional sequence had a flip angle of 90°, FOV of 240 × 240 mm2, matrix of 64 × 64, slice thickness of 4 mm, and slice interval of 0.8 mm. Visual stimuli were presented through goggles mounted on the head coil.

instrument.value: Siemens 3T Tim Trio MRI system (Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: A T1-weighted MPRAGE structural image was acquired with slice thickness of 4 mm, FOV of 240 × 240 × 240 mm3, and matrix of 256 × 256 × 256.

The first trial of each block was discarded. Remaining volumes were corrected for slice timing, realigned to the mean volume to correct for head motion, spatially normalized to standard MNI space using a 12-parameter affine transformation, and smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: The first trial of each block was discarded to reach magnetization equilibrium.
Realignment to the mean volume to correct for head motion
Spatial normalization to standard MNI space using a 12-parameter affine transformation
Spatial smoothing with an 8-mm full-width at half-maximum isotropic Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: Each condition was modeled using a box-car function convolved with a canonical HRF. Realignment parameters were included as covariates of no interest.

Group, emotion and ER were entered as between-subject factors and BIS/BAS subscale scores as covariates; interactive effects between group and motivation and the main effect of group on emotion regulation were examined.

BIS/BAS scores were entered into a generalized linear regression model to predict reappraisal-related brain activation; ROI time courses were generated by extracting the first eigenvariate of 8 mm around peak voxels using REX.

title.value: Motivational dispositions Predict Reappraisal-related Brain Activity in functional ROIs

footer.value: BIS/BAS scores were entered into a generalized linear regression model to predict reappraisal-related brain activation. Functional ROI time courses (beta values) under each condition in each group were generated by extracting the first eigenvariate of 8 mm around the peak voxels of respective clusters with no scaling, using a Matlab package REX (Response Exploration). BBS, BIS/BAS scale; L, left hemisphere; R, right hemisphere. ** P < 0.01.
